analysis.title: the squeeze nobody is positioned for
key_insights: SPX cash is trading at its longer-term trendline and the 200-day moving average, and remains inside the range in place since May.
NDX futures printed their biggest upside candle since the latest sell-off, bouncing off a long-term trendline with the potential for a second higher low.
VIX has overshot the move in SPX. With Thanksgiving approaching, a modest pause in selling could push volatility lower and help stabilize markets.
The gap between VXN and VIX is not new, but a fade in tech fear, even a slight one, is flagged as a risk to the current positioning.

NDX has sold off sharply over recent weeks while several major CDS spreads tightened. The note recalls that summer CDS stress spilled over into tech and asks whether that dynamic could now reverse in a mini rally.

Fundamental long/short funds are cutting exposure. Gross leverage fell 4.4 points in November to 206.3% (23rd percentile over the past year). Net leverage fell 7.6 points to 41.6%, the lowest in five years (GS data).

Hedge funds are selling global tech at the fastest pace in a decade on a trailing six-week basis, with a -4.4 z-score. The global tech long/short ratio fell from a YTD peak of 2.9 to 1.79, near 10-year lows (GS data).
Nomura estimates aggregate SPX dealer gamma at about negative $7.3bn, near the bottom of its historical range. Negative gamma can amplify moves in either direction, including a squeeze higher.
Poor liquidity amplifies moves both ways. With dealers deeply short gamma, a squeeze higher could be magnified by thin liquidity (GS).
NDX seasonality points to one final push higher into year-end.

sector_views.rationale: Hedge fund tech selling is at a decade extreme and tech fear (VXN) is elevated, which the note frames as a setup for a squeeze if selling pauses. No explicit rating is given.

risk_factors: Negative dealer gamma amplifies moves in both directions, including further downside.
Thin liquidity can magnify a squeeze or a further sell-off.
SPX sits at its trendline and 200-day moving average, so a break would end the range in place since May.
Tech fear and CDS stress could re-intensify.
vol_and_positioning: VIX has overshot the move in SPX and fear remains elevated. A pause in selling around Thanksgiving could lower volatility.
The VXN-VIX gap persists. A modest fade in tech fear is flagged as a catalyst for a reversal.
Fundamental L/S gross leverage is 206.3% (23rd percentile over one year), down 4.4 points in November. Net leverage is 41.6%, down 7.6 points and the lowest in five years (GS).
Global tech hedge fund selling over six weeks has a -4.4 z-score, the most aggressive in a decade. The tech L/S ratio is 1.79, down from a 2.9 YTD peak (GS).
Aggregate SPX dealer gamma is about -$7.3bn per Nomura, near the bottom of its historical range. Thin liquidity could amplify a squeeze higher.

tension_points.bull_case: Hedge fund tech selling is at a decade extreme, net leverage is at a five-year low, and VIX has overshot SPX. A pause in selling, helped by Thanksgiving and seasonality, could trigger a squeeze amplified by negative dealer gamma (-$7.3bn) and thin liquidity.
tension_points.bear_case: Negative gamma and poor liquidity also amplify downside. SPX is at its trendline and 200-day average, and tech fear and CDS stress remain elevated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A break of the SPX trendline and 200-day moving average, which the note identifies as the current support area.
